item.title: Miwa Somen: The Birthplace of Japan's Thin Noodles — Guide
item.description: The Miwa region around Sakurai, at the foot of sacred Mount Miwa, is considered the birthplace of somen, the ultra-thin white wheat noodles now eaten across Japan. Local tradition holds that noodle-making began here some 1,200 years ago near Omiwa Shrine, and the area’s makers still hand-stretch the dough into fine threads dried in the winter air, a craft prized for its delicate, firm texture. Miwa somen is enjoyed two ways: chilled and dipped in cold tsuyu on hot summer days (sometimes as flowing nagashi-somen caught from bamboo flumes), or warm in a soothing nyumen broth in the colder months.
